newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati left off election roll.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati left off election roll.

text.p: Indonesia's ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri was left out in the cold on Monday when the country's three legally-recognised parties submitted their candidates for next year's general elections.

Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno and currently a member of parliament, was ousted as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) by a government- backed faction in June.

Megawati, who has become the chief symbol of dissent against President Suharto's government, was not on the list of PDI candidates submitted by the man who replaced her, deputy parliament speaker Surjadi.
Asked by reporters if Megawati was on his list, Surjadi said: "No."
However, he said there were four or five members of her faction included from PDI branches on the resort island of Bali, from Jambi in central Sumatra, and Maluku in eastern Indonesia.
Representatives of Megawati's faction of the PDI were rebuffed by electoral officials when they later tried to submit their own list of 750 candidates for the polls.

One of the representatives, Kwik Kian Gie, said the faction might take the government to court for the right to run in the elections, but added: "We have not yet decided whether to start another suit".
Megawati has already taken legal action against the government and political rivals to reverse the decision of the June congress to depose her as party leader. The suit is currently before the court.

The Christian-nationalist PDI officially put forward 903 candidates for the elections to the 500-seat national assembly. Voters elect 425 members and the armed forces, whose members do not vote, appoint the remainder.
The ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) each submitted 850 candidates. All candidates have still to be vetted and officially approved.
Golkar's candidates include two of President Suharto's children and a son of Vice-President Try Sutrisno.
Memed said there were 124,740,978 registered voters out of a population of 196,286,613. Regional and municipal elections will be held concurrently with the national poll.
Golkar won 68 percent of the vote in the last general elections in 1992, the PPP 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.

Political analysts have said the government wanted Megawati out as PDI leader for fear she could draw votes from Golkar next year. There was also concern she might run against President Suharto in 1998.
Suharto, who replaced Sukarno in the mid-1960s, has been elected unopposed for six consecutive terms.
Police on July 27 evicted her supporters from the PDI headquarters building, sparking the worst riots Jakarta has seen in more than two decades in which at least five people died.
Megawati set up a rival headquarters this month, but the powerful military said neither she nor her followers had the right to conduct political activities.
Home Affairs Minister Yogie Memed said at Monday's nomination ceremony that the representatives of the people should understand the aspirations of the people.
There would be change in Indonesia, he added, "but that does not mean they will be revolutionary changes."
